link_fixes.original_markdown: Release on touch end and cancellation as well as ordinary key up. Retry a rejected release twice at 16 ms outside the audio callback, then shut down and report failure if publication remains blocked. Cancel retries during teardown. The [held motor example](examples.md#sustained-game-motor) implements this ownership policy. For pause/owner close, invalidate app scheduling and shut down; require a new start before future notes.

link_fixes.original_markdown: The native transport uses 1 to 512 sixteenth-note steps, each with `notes: [60, 64, 67]` (integer MIDI 12 to 119) or `rest: true`. A gate from 0.01 to 1 sets release onset within the swung step. Voice shaping belongs in root `voice`; per-step `overrides` merge into it. Native sequence steps do not accept pattern `duration`, `noteValue` or sweep-end keys. There are no ties or independent tracks. The [sequence example](examples.md#native-sequence-with-chords-and-edits) shows playback, edits, polling and cleanup.

link_fixes.original_markdown: `setMasterProcessing` merges partial updates, validates the entire result and returns publication acceptance. Continuous controls ramp over 10 ms. Disabling an effect closes input gradually and keeps its tail, bounded to 30 seconds with a final fade, then restores exact bypass. It does not undo a non-unity input gain. `stopAll` invalidates histories and stops the native sequence; `shutdown` also cancels timer patterns and frees the stream/buffers. See the [processing example](examples.md#chorus-delay-reverb-and-creative-saturation) and [field ranges](api.md#setmasterprocessingoptions).

link_fixes.original_markdown: Choose a held voice when the ending follows a player action instead of a fixed duration: motor, charge beam, pad or the last chord of a ceremony. `noteOn` starts a positive app-owned ID; `noteOff` begins release from the current level, and compatible `updateVoice` edits ramp over 10 ms. Distinct IDs remain independent events with fixed gain. Reserve enough capacity for their releases and unrelated effects, and release on cancellation as well as ordinary key up. See the [held motor recipe](examples.md#sustained-game-motor) for retry/cleanup handling.

link_fixes.original_markdown: All processors are off initially, with fixed input gain 1. Activate them explicitly through `setMasterProcessing` on a running engine; [copyable configuration](examples.md#chorus-delay-reverb-and-creative-saturation) and [exact ranges](api.md#setmasterprocessingoptions) are available. The shared chain affects every simultaneous sound. A subtle reverb can enrich a result chord, while many wet collisions can obscure short gameplay feedback. There are no per-voice sends or separate music/effects buses.

link_fixes.original_markdown: The two additional voice LFOs move filter cutoff, square PWM or sine FM index using sine/triangle shapes. Cutoff movement creates slow breathing or rhythmic filtering; PWM adds changing harmonic color; a small FM-index modulation varies brightness. Free rates reach 20 Hz, and synced rates follow native transport tempo. These slots are separate from pitch vibrato. Avoid deep/high-rate modulation with strong resonance or high-frequency FM; safe parameter clamping does not guarantee a pleasant or alias-free sound. The [two-LFO example](examples.md#two-voice-lfos) shows a filtered PWM pad.

link_fixes.original_markdown: The event arrives when the pattern ends, about 1 ms after the sum of its step lengths, not when you call. A 30 second pattern reports after 30 seconds. Swing and FIR draining can leave sound after completion; the event does not certify audible silence. The [interactive example](../example/README.md#pattern-completion-and-replacement) demonstrates completion, replacement and shutdown.
